themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks surged to 90 THIS WEEK, up 304% from the 22.2-weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden and acute quality-of-life disruption affecting outdoor spaces across Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 90 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 22.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (304% spike, z-score: 5.93)
Represents the single largest percentage spike in 311 data for the district this week
Distinct from residential noise complaints (1,805 over 90 days), suggesting concentrated outdoor/commercial source
reporting_angles: Door-knock interviews with residents on which blocks are most affected and at what times of day
Investigation into whether nightlife venues, street fairs, construction, or vehicle traffic caused the sudden increase
Review of 311 complaint geotags to identify hotspot blocks and cross-reference with liquor licenses or active construction permits

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Ubers, Lyfts, etc.) jumped to 32 THIS WEEK, up 144% from the 13.1-weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling rapid deterioration in rideshare traffic management or illegal activity in the district.
evidence: 32 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (144% spike, z-score: 7.97)
Second-most statistically anomalous spike in this week's data
Timing coincides with major downtown transit patterns and potential surge-pricing or congestion events
reporting_angles: Interview TLC and Uber/Lyft to determine if there was a surge in service requests or driver influx this week
Query 311 complaint summaries to categorize nature of complaints: illegal stopping, double-parking, noise, passenger conflicts, or driver misconduct
Check if any major events or transit disruptions occurred that could have redirected rideshare traffic to the district

themes_detail.label: Dangerous sidewalk conditions
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints peaked at 22 three weeks ago (193% above the 7.5-weekly baseline), representing the longest-running high-severity spike in the dataset and indicating sustained infrastructure neglect affecting pedestrian safety across the district.
evidence: 22 sidewalk condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (193% spike, z-score: 9.67)
Highest z-score of all spikes, indicating the most statistically extreme deviation from baseline
Street condition complaints also spiked last week to 72 (229% above 21.9 weekly average, z-score: 5.09), suggesting broader pavement/infrastructure crisis
reporting_angles: Visual survey of major streets and avenues in both Fort Greene and Brooklyn Heights to document trip hazards, potholes, broken slabs
FOIL request for Department of Transportation repair backlog and timeline for sidewalk resurfacing in this community district
Interview seniors, parents with strollers, and disability advocates about accessibility risks posed by deteriorating sidewalks

themes_detail.label: Construction contamination concerns
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, up 540% from the 0.6-weekly average, coinciding with elevated building permit filings (1,162 in last 90 days, including 87 new buildings and 835 alterations) and signaling potential lead hazard exposure during renovation season.
evidence: 4 construction lead dust complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
1,162 total building permits filed in last 90 days; 835 alterations (many likely involving pre-1978 buildings with lead paint risk)
Building/use violations also surged to 7 last week (460% above 1.2 weekly average, z-score: 5.94), suggesting code compliance issues on active sites
reporting_angles: Identify which specific construction projects (by block/address from DOB permits) are generating lead dust complaints and whether contractors are certified in lead-safe work practices
Investigate whether Department of Housing Preservation and Development and DEP are adequately monitoring lead-based paint removal during alterations to 1950s-era brownstones and apartment buildings
Interview families and schools near active construction sites about respiratory concerns and air quality; request recent lead testing results from NYCDEP

themes_detail.label: Real estate enforcement spike
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints surged to 7 last week, up 1020% from the 0.6-weekly baseline, the most extreme percentage spike in the entire dataset, indicating either a sudden enforcement action by city agencies or a novel complaint category requiring urgent clarification.
evidence: 7 real-time enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1020% spike, z-score: 6.43)
Largest percentage spike across all 311 categories, but baseline is extremely low (nearly zero), suggesting either new complaint type or specific enforcement campaign
No supporting data on what 'real-time enforcement' category captures; 311 system definition unclear
reporting_angles: Contact 311 and CPIO to obtain full text summaries of the 7 real-time enforcement complaints to understand what issue is being reported
Determine whether this is a new or re-categorized 311 complaint type that explains the historical near-zero baseline
If related to a specific city agency action (NYPD, DOE, DOE, FDNY, etc.), request statement on any enforcement operations launched in the district last week
